headline: Dubai developers shift to selective positioning at International Property Show
deck: The International Property Show closed with 300 exhibitors, floor space up 38 per cent, and a sales pitch that has moved from scarcity to selectivity.
excerpt: The International Property Show closed in Dubai on 9 September with more than 300 exhibitors and exhibition space up 38 per cent on last year, but a noticeably changed pitch from developers.
content:
The International Property Show closed at Dubai World Trade Centre on 9 September, its twenty-second edition, with more than 300 exhibitors and exhibition space up 38 per cent on the 2025 event. The Dubai Land Department is the show's strategic partner, and the floor was organised around five declared pillars: real estate, future cities, proptech and startups, design, and services.

The exhibitor list was weighted toward Dubai's mid-market and volume developers — Azizi Properties, Binghatti, Danube, Fakhruddin Properties, SanZen and Union Properties, with Peace Homes Development as platinum sponsor and Prestige One Developments, Holm Developers and ANAX Developments also on the floor. That composition is itself the story. A show floor dominated by the developers who sell units rather than the ones who sell trophies is a floor pitched at absorption rather than at records.

Dawood Al Shezawi, president of the show, described it as the marketplace where global institutional capital meets Dubai's development landscape, and separately framed the event's focus as industrial investment spanning real estate, artificial intelligence and technology. The framing is broader than a property show would have used two years ago, and it tracks a market where the marginal buyer is increasingly an institution allocating across asset classes rather than an individual buying a second home.

The clearest signal from the floor was in what developers were prepared to concede on terms. Several offered zero-down-payment structures with monthly instalments at 1.5 per cent over sixty months, and the stock on show skewed toward affordable and mid-range product rather than the premium tier. Developers described the market in terms of selectivity and sustainability rather than momentum. Sergey Avayan, founder of Holm Developers, put the requirement on developers themselves, saying they need to be more creative.

Payment terms of that structure do real work in a softening market. They move the buyer's constraint from deposit capital to monthly income, which widens the addressable pool without cutting the headline price — a developer can hold nominal pricing while materially reducing the cost of entry. It is the standard response to lengthening absorption, and it usually appears before published prices move.

Attendance figures for the 2026 edition should be treated with care. One outlet reported 35,000 participants from 190 countries; the organiser's own pre-show material projected well over 30,000; the audited 2025 result was 30,719 from 153 countries. The higher figure appears in a single source and has not been corroborated. No project launches with values, unit counts or locations were announced during the show, and no transaction total or memorandum count has been published for this edition — the 2025 comparators of 50 memoranda and more than AED 500m in documented transactions remain the only figures on record.
